column9: CALIBRATION: (1) THE PACE LINE WAS RIGHT AND THE PICK IGNORED IT: 'the leader is likely Pride Of Arras with Gethin on his quarters; Gethin PULLS' — on Polytrack at 1m4f in a 5-runner race the dictating G2 winner is the best horse; the sheet had it; the verdict did not use it. (2) ODDS-ON IN A GROUP 3 ON THE ALL-WEATHER: the rulebook's #14 AW caution and the odds-on bar both said no bet; I stated them and picked anyway 'to test whether I can name the winner' — I could not, and the record now holds the receipt: the cautions are the method, not decoration. (3) THE DANGER-BY-NAME: Constitution Hill got the danger slot because of who he is on a Tuesday at Cheltenham, not what the figures said he is on a Saturday at Kempton; the Ascot 2:10 lesson (Heyzoom, the danger by sire) repeated in the same hour. (4) THE THIRD 'WHAT WOULD MAKE ME WRONG' TO COME TRUE TODAY (Haydock: the ground/the champion's engine — First Law; Ascot: the 7lb rise — bit; Kempton: the pace — Pride Of Arras): from the next sitting that line is written BEFORE the verdict and if it names a horse, that horse's decisive line is weighed against the pick's decisive line on the page, in two sentences, and the stronger one is the pick — no more picking against my own scenario.
